title: The Climate-Pollution Convergence
subtitle: Interconnected Environmental Risks and the Future of Human Exposure

contribution: Develops the concept of Climate-Pollution Convergence—originated by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics—analyzing how climate pressures and pollution pressures interact through shared sources and atmospheric feedback loops to compound human exposure, and how integrated risk reduction strengthens Polycrisis Resilience.
abstract:
The Climate-Pollution Convergence is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It examines how climate-related hazards, atmospheric pollution, environmental degradation, and socioeconomic conditions interact to shape present and future patterns of human exposure—and demonstrates how integrated risk reduction strengthens long-term Polycrisis Resilience.

keyFindings.title: Climate change and pollution must be understood as convergent environmental risks because their shared combustion sources, atmospheric interactions, and overlapping human exposures amplify vulnerability beyond either pressure considered independently.

Atmospheric and ecological feedback loops—such as warming accelerating ground-level ozone formation and drought-driven wildfires injecting massive PM2.5 plumes—compound cardiopulmonary morbidity to 59.0% above single-hazard baselines.

The distribution of climate-pollution exposure is shaped not only by environmental change, but also by economic development, urbanization, infrastructure quality, technological access, and adaptive capacity.

Integrated approaches uniting clean energy transitions, pollution prevention, climate adaptation, environmental infrastructure, and technology diffusion cut composite exposure from 65.0 (2025) to 9.5 by 2100 (-85.4%) while delivering 7.5x–11.2x social benefit-cost ratios.
